prompt: Pull the code and reason phrase out of an HTTP status line and classify the code by its leading digit. Complete the four methods in StatusLineReader.
explanation: A status line has exactly three fields, but the last one may contain spaces, so split with a limit of 3 rather than splitting on every space. Anything that fails the checks -- no HTTP/ prefix, too few fields, a non-numeric code -- reports the sentinel -1 instead of throwing, which keeps callers simple. The classification is driven entirely by the code's hundreds digit, the convention every HTTP client relies on to decide whether to follow, retry, or give up.
hints: line.split(" ", 3) keeps the reason phrase in one piece as the third element.
Wrap Integer.parseInt in try/catch and return -1 from the catch block -- that is cleaner than checking every character yourself.
reasonPhrase can reuse statusCode to decide whether the line is valid at all before it looks for a third field.
